summary: Iteration 26: Verified refactor regression (4 split routers: meetings/smtp_config/sfu_config/rtc_config) and NEW P2 features N8N run history + MCP tools listing. Backend 12/12 pytest tests pass; UI Run modal shows history rows after triggering N8N workflow; MCP modal gracefully shows 'No tools' for non-MCP endpoint. Found and FIXED one UI bug: RunModal & McpModal useEffect returned a Promise, causing 'destroy is not a function' pageerror that crashed the modal (and blanked the connected list) on close.

ui_bugs.issue: useEffect(loadRuns, []) and useEffect(loadTools, []) passed a function returning a Promise, triggering React pageerror 'destroy is not a function' on unmount, crashing the modal and unmounting the connected list. FIXED by wrapping calls: useEffect(() => { loadRuns(); }, []).

action_items: Verify the two-line useEffect fix in /app/frontend/src/pages/Integrations.jsx (RunModal L217, McpModal L288). Consider adding a global React error boundary around modals so a single crash doesn't unmount the whole page tree.

Non-blocking: mcp/tools endpoint returns 200 {tools:[]} when hitting a non-MCP endpoint that responds with a non-JSONRPC body — good graceful behavior; consider returning a soft warning field so UI can distinguish 'no tools' vs 'server not MCP' someday.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/meetings.py imports helpers from routers.smtp_config (build_ics, send_meeting_email) — a router importing another router is a slight layering smell. Consider moving build_ics + send_meeting_email to a shared services/email module.
routers/rtc_config.py imports _get_livekit_cfg from routers.sfu_config — same cross-router coupling. Extract a services layer to avoid tight coupling between router modules.

Integrations.jsx: any useEffect that calls an async function should either be `useEffect(() => { fn(); }, [])` or declare fn inside. React already warned about this pattern in console; enforce with eslint-plugin-react-hooks rule react-hooks/exhaustive-deps.

mcp_call_tool records failures on both HTTPException path and generic Exception path but then re-raises — good; ensure _record_run cap-to-50 pruning uses a proper index on integration_runs.integration_id + created_at (avoids O(N) delete_many on high-run integrations).

MCP tools/list against non-MCP https://httpbin.org/status/200 returns 200 {tools:[]} and UI shows mcp-empty gracefully. Fixed React useEffect Promise-return bug in RunModal & McpModal.
rca of the issue: RCA — 'destroy is not a function' pageerror: RunModal L217 had `useEffect(loadRuns, [])` where loadRuns is `() => api.get(...).then(...).catch(...)`, i.e. returns a Promise. React expects useEffect callback to return either undefined or a cleanup FUNCTION. When the effect runs, React captures the returned Promise and treats it as a cleanup function; on unmount (modal close) it calls `cleanup()` which is `promise` and then `promise.destroy()` — crashing the component and (without an error boundary) tearing down the parent tree so the connected integrations list disappeared. Reproduction: open /integrations with any n8n integration, click Run, close the modal → the connected list vanishes and console shows PAGEERROR: destroy is not a function. Fix: wrap in arrow function — `useEffect(() => { loadRuns(); }, [])`. Same fix applied to McpModal. Verified: cards remained (4/4) after opening & closing both modals; no pageerror in console.
